Next I’m checking the policy’s general eligibility section and whether any change notices amend this document, so I can give you the current criteria accurately.## General eligibility criteria for CAP/DA services

Under current **Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2 (CAP/DA)**, NC Medicaid covers CAP/DA when the beneficiary meets the policy’s Medicaid and waiver-specific criteria. In plain language, the person generally must:

- **Be enrolled in NC Medicaid**
- **Be in Medicaid Direct (fee-for-service)** for CAP/DA participation
- **Be age 18 or older**
- **Need a nursing-facility level of care**, as determined by NC Medicaid
- **Need long-term care supports** related to a documented medical diagnosis and functional care need
- **Have a reasonable indication of need for at least one CAP/DA home- and community-based service within 30 calendar days of evaluation**
- **Be in a CAP/DA target group** documented in the approved waiver application
- **Meet applicable Medicaid eligibility criteria**
- **Choose waiver participation** rather than institutional care (freedom of choice)
- **Be assigned a CAP/DA waiver slot**
- **Have an approved and signed service plan** authorizing one or more waiver services on a monthly basis  
  - or, for certain short-term equipment/modification/technology needs, a signed service plan authorizing that support so the person can return to or remain in the primary private residence and avoid institutional placement
- **Be able to maintain health, safety, and well-being** in the primary private residence or other approved location with formal and informal supports
- **Have paid care needs that can be maintained within the average institutional cost of the CAP/DA waiver**
- **Have a primary physician** who can link and coordinate medical services
- **Have an emergency back-up and disaster plan** identifying who will provide care if direct-care staff are unavailable, the primary caregiver has an emergency, or there is a public health emergency

**Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2, Section 3.2.1 — “Specific criteria covered by Medicaid”** states that Medicaid covers CAP/DA when the beneficiary meets criteria including nursing facility level of care, reasonable indication of need for at least one HCBS service within 30 days, a signed service plan, ability to remain safely at home or an approved location with supports, care costs within the average institutional cost, a primary physician, and an emergency back-up/disaster plan. Effective date: **September 1, 2025**. Source: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

**Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2, unnumbered section “a. Medicaid” within the eligibility provisions** adds that the person:
- is enrolled in **fee-for-service (Medicaid Direct)**;
- requires institutional level of care under the NC State Medicaid Plan;
- is a member of a waiver target group;
- meets applicable Medicaid eligibility criteria;
- exercises freedom of choice to enter or remain in the waiver;
- is assigned a CAP/DA waiver slot;
- can have health, safety, and well-being maintained at home or an approved location with formal and informal supports; and
- **is age 18 years old and older**. Effective date: **September 1, 2025**. Source: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

**Clinical Coverage Policy 3K-2, Section 2.1.1 — “General”** also states that an eligible beneficiary must be enrolled in the NC Medicaid program, and notes that service restrictions tied to the beneficiary’s eligibility category may make them ineligible for this service. Effective date: **September 1, 2025**. Source: [Community Alternatives Program for Disabled Adults (CAP/DA)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3k-2-community-alternatives-program-disabled-adults-capda/download?attachment)

For a person to qualify for **CAP/DA**, the policy requires more than just Medicaid enrollment. The person must be an **adult in Medicaid Direct**, meet **nursing-facility level of care**, need at least one **CAP/DA service**, be able to live safely in the community with supports, have an **approved service plan**, and fit within waiver rules like **slot availability** and **cost limits**.

per_question.question: What DME items are specifically NOT covered by NC Medicaid under the Orthotics and Prosthetics policy, and what general criteria must be met for coverage?
per_question.agent_answer:

Next I’m pulling the full text of those sections and checking for amendments before answering.Under **NC Medicaid Clinical Coverage Policy 5B (Orthotics & Prosthetics)**, the following items are **specifically not covered**:

- **Devices for the beneficiary’s comfort or convenience**, or for the convenience of the beneficiary’s caregiver(s)
- **Backup devices** or **duplicate devices** to keep at different locations
- **Devices and supplies for residents of nursing facilities**
- **Devices or supplies covered by another agency**
- **Equipment or supplies for beneficiaries receiving hospice care**, as defined in the policy’s care-coordination subsection

Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 5B, Section 4.2.1 — "Specific Criteria Not Covered by Medicaid"**  
[Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

There are also **general non-coverage rules**. Medicaid does not cover the item/service if:

- the beneficiary does **not** meet the **eligibility requirements** in Section 2.0;
- the beneficiary does **not** meet the **criteria** in Section 3.0;
- the item/service **duplicates another provider’s** product or service; or
- the item/service is **experimental, investigational, or part of a clinical trial**

Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 5B, Section 4.1 — "General Criteria Not Covered"**  
[Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

## General criteria that must be met for coverage

At the general level, the procedure, product, or service must be:

- **individualized, specific, and consistent** with the beneficiary’s symptoms or confirmed diagnosis, and **not in excess of the beneficiary’s needs**;
- able to be **safely furnished**, with **no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment available statewide**; and
- furnished in a way **not primarily intended for the convenience** of the beneficiary, caretaker, or provider

Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 5B, Section 3.1 — "General Criteria Covered"**  
[Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

## Additional orthotics/prosthetics-specific coverage criteria

For orthotics and prosthetics specifically, Medicaid requires that they:

- be **ordered by a physician, physician assistant, or nurse practitioner**;
- be **medically necessary** to maintain or improve the beneficiary’s medical, physical, or functional level, and appropriate for use in a **noninstitutional setting** where normal life activities occur;
- be supported by a **documented face-to-face encounter** with the ordering clinician, occurring **no more than six months before** initiation of the orthotic/prosthetic;
- have the beneficiary’s need **reviewed at least annually** by the ordering clinician;
- be a **reasonable and medically necessary part of the treatment plan**;
- be **consistent with the diagnosis and medical condition**, especially the beneficiary’s functional limitations and symptoms; and
- be **of high quality**, with replacement parts available and obtainable

The policy further states:

- **Orthotic devices** are medically necessary when required to **correct or prevent skeletal deformities**, **support or align movable body parts**, or **preserve or improve physical function**.
- **Prosthetic devices** are medically necessary as a replacement for all or part of the function of a **permanently inoperative, absent, or malfunctioning body part**, and the beneficiary must require the prosthesis for **mobility, daily care, or rehabilitation purposes**.

Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 5B, Section 3.2.1 — "Specific criteria covered by Medicaid"**  
[Orthotics & Prosthetics](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/5b-orthotics-prosthetics/download?attachment)

## Bottom line

**Not covered:** comfort/convenience items, backups/duplicates, nursing-facility resident devices/supplies, items another agency covers, and hospice-related equipment/supplies under the policy.  
**Covered only if:** the item is medically necessary, properly ordered, tied to the beneficiary’s diagnosis and treatment plan, not duplicative or experimental, and supported by the required clinical encounter and ongoing review.

I’m pulling that full text now so I can give you the complete entrance, continued-service, and discharge standards from the current version of Policy 8C.## Outpatient behavioral health criteria in NC Medicaid

For **outpatient behavioral health services provided by direct-enrolled providers**, the governing source is **Clinical Coverage Policy 8C**, effective **April 15, 2025**. Based on the current policy text, the criteria are:

### 1. Entrance criteria
A beneficiary must meet **all** of these requirements:

- Have a **current DSM-5 diagnosis**;
- Present **behavioral, psychological, or biological dysfunction and functional impairment** consistent with and associated with that diagnosis;
- If a **higher level of care is indicated but unavailable**, or the beneficiary is **refusing that service**, outpatient services may be provided **until the appropriate level of care is available** or **to support the beneficiary to participate in that higher level of care**;
- Be **capable of developing skills to manage symptoms, make behavioral changes, and respond favorably to therapeutic interventions**; and
- There must be **no evidence that alternative interventions would be more effective**, based on North Carolina community practice standards.

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 8C, Section 3.2.1.1 — “Entrance Criteria” (effective Apr. 15, 2025): [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

### 2. Continued service criteria
The beneficiary must meet:

#### A. **Any one** of the following:
- The desired outcome or level of functioning **has not been restored, improved, or sustained** over the timeframe in the treatment plan;
- The beneficiary **continues to be at risk for relapse** based on current clinical assessment and history; **or**
- There is a **tenuous nature of the functional gains**.

#### B. And, **in addition to A, any one** of the following:
- The beneficiary has **achieved current treatment plan goals**, and **additional goals are indicated** as evidenced by documented symptoms; **or**
- The beneficiary is **making satisfactory progress toward meeting goals** and there is documentation that supports that.

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 8C, Section 3.2.1.2 — “Continued Service Criteria” (effective Apr. 15, 2025): [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

### 3. Discharge criteria
Discharge is appropriate if **any one** of the following applies:

- The beneficiary’s **level of functioning has improved** with respect to the goals in the treatment plan;
- The beneficiary or legally responsible person **no longer wishes to receive the services**; **or**
- The beneficiary, based on presentation and **failure to show improvement despite modifications in the treatment plan**, **requires a more appropriate best practice or evidence-based treatment modality** under North Carolina community practice standards.

**Citation:** Clinical Coverage Policy 8C, Section 3.2.1.3 — “Discharge Criteria” (effective Apr. 15, 2025): [8C, Outpatient Behavioral Health Services Provided by Direct-Enrolled Providers](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8c-outpatient-behavioral-health-services-provided-direct-enrolled-providers/download?attachment)

## Plain-language summary
NC Medicaid’s outpatient behavioral health policy generally requires:

- A **current mental health diagnosis**,
- Symptoms and **functional impairment tied to that diagnosis**,
- A reasonable expectation the person can **benefit from outpatient treatment**,
- Continued treatment only when the person still needs it and is either **still at risk**, **not yet stabilized**, or **still progressing toward or adding treatment goals**, and
- Discharge when the person has **met goals**, **does not want services**, or **needs a different level or type of treatment**.

per_question.question: Does NC Medicaid cover Personal Care Services for beneficiaries who live in an assisted living facility?
per_question.agent_answer:

I’m now reading the scope/general eligibility and the not-covered congregate-facility section, and then I’ll verify amendments.Yes — **NC Medicaid does cover Personal Care Services (PCS) for some beneficiaries who live in assisted living-type facilities**, but the governing policy is **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1**, not the ordinary in-home PCS policy.

## Short answer
PCS can be covered for a beneficiary who lives in an **Adult Care Home (ACH)**, **combination home**, or certain **group homes**, if the beneficiary meets the policy’s functional and medical criteria and the setting/provider requirements. Assisted living facilities are generally analyzed under this **congregate settings** PCS policy.  
Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, Section 3.2.1 — "Specific criteria covered by Medicaid"** and **Section 3.3 — "Personal Care Services"**: [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

## Why I’m using Policy 3L-1 and not 3L
- **Policy 3L** is the general State Plan PCS policy for **in-home settings**; its service section is titled **"Personal Care Services in In-Home Settings."**
- **Policy 3L-1** is specifically titled **"State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings."**

So for a person in an assisted living facility / adult care home, **3L-1 is the matching policy**, and **3L is not the primary source** because it applies to in-home PCS rather than congregate residential settings.  
Sources: **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L** (title and Section 3.3 title) and **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1** (title): [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS)](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3l-state-plan-personal-care-services-pcs/download?attachment); [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

## What has to be true for coverage
Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, Section 3.2.1**, the beneficiary must:

- have a **medical or mental condition, disability, or cognitive impairment**; and
- show unmet needs for at least:
  - **three of the five qualifying ADLs with limited hands-on assistance**, or
  - **two ADLs, one requiring extensive assistance**, or
  - **two ADLs, one requiring full dependence assistance**; and
- **reside in**:
  - a North Carolina-licensed **Adult Care Home (ACH)**,
  - a **combination home**, or
  - a qualifying licensed **group home**.

That same section also says these additional criteria must be met, including:

- the congregate setting must be **safe and free of health hazards**;
- the setting must have had the required **inspection**;
- **no other third-party payer** is responsible for PCS;
- **no family/household member or other informal caregiver** is available, willing, and able to provide the authorized services during the time PCS is provided;
- the PCS must be **directly linked** to a documented medical/mental condition or physical/cognitive impairment;
- the beneficiary must be under the **ongoing direct care of a physician** for the condition causing the functional limits; and
- the beneficiary must be **medically stable** and **must not require continuous care, monitoring, or supervision by a licensed nurse or other licensed health care professional**.  
Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, Section 3.2.1 — "Specific criteria covered by Medicaid"**: [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

## What services are covered
Under **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, Section 3.3**, Medicaid covers PCS occurring **at minimum, once per week**, including:

- hands-on assistance with qualifying ADLs;
- set-up, supervision, cueing, prompting, and guiding when provided as part of the hands-on ADL assistance;
- assistance with home-management IADLs directly related to qualifying ADLs and essential to care at the private residence;
- medication assistance tied to a documented condition/impairment;
- help with adaptive or assistive devices linked to qualifying ADLs;
- help using durable medical equipment linked to qualifying ADLs; and
- special assistance / delegated medical monitoring tasks.  
Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, Section 3.3 — "Personal Care Services"**: [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

## Important exclusions
Even in a licensed congregate facility, PCS is not covered for a beneficiary who:

- is **ventilator dependent**;
- **requires continuous licensed nursing care**;
- has a physician certification that the placement is **no longer appropriate**;
- has health needs that **cannot be met in that specific licensed care home**; or
- has other medical/functional care needs that **cannot be properly met in a licensed care home** under NC law and licensure rules.  
Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1, Section 4.2.1.1 — "Licensed Congregate Facility"**: [State Plan Personal Care Services (PCS) Provided in Congregate Settings](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/14986/download?attachment)

## Bottom line
**Yes, NC Medicaid can cover PCS for someone living in an assisted living / adult care home setting**, but only through **Clinical Coverage Policy 3L-1** and only if the beneficiary meets the policy’s **ADL, medical necessity, residence, and setting-safety requirements**.

## Coverage criteria for CAR-T cell therapy

A beneficiary must first meet the policy’s **general coverage criteria**. The service must be:

- **individualized, specific, and consistent with symptoms or confirmed diagnosis**, and **not in excess of the beneficiary’s needs**;
- able to be **safely furnished**, with **no equally effective and more conservative or less costly treatment available statewide**; and
- furnished in a manner **not primarily intended for the convenience** of the beneficiary, caretaker, or provider.

- the **CAR-T therapy has received FDA approval**;
- it is administered **according to FDA-approved guidelines** for:
  - **indications and usage**;
  - **dosage and administration**;
  - **dosage forms and strengths**; and
  - **warnings and precautions**; and
- it is administered at a **certified or authorized treatment center**.

If the product is subject to a **REMS program**, then:

- the treatment center **must be enrolled in the REMS**, and
- providers **must be trained to manage cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and neurological toxicities**.

Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 11A-17, Section 3.2.1 — “Specific criteria covered by Medicaid”** [CAR-T Cell Therapy](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)

The provider-certification section adds that hospitals and associated clinics dispensing CAR-T must have:

- **special certification**; and
- **on-site, immediate access to tocilizumab**;

and those who prescribe, dispense, or administer CAR-T must be aware of how to manage:

- **cytokine release syndrome**; and
- **neurological toxicities**.

The policy requires a **prior approval request** plus **all health records and other records supporting that the beneficiary meets Section 3.2 criteria**.  
Source: **Clinical Coverage Policy 11A-17, Section 5.2.1 — “General”** [CAR-T Cell Therapy](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/11a-17-car-t-cell-therapy/download?attachment)
